name: Mahabodhi Temple Complex, Bodh Gaya
path: Mahabodhi Temple Complex, Bodh Gaya, Gaya, India
summary: Holiest site in Buddhism where Prince Siddhartha Gautama attained supreme Enlightenment.
points: Original temple built by Emperor Ashoka c. 250 BCE; grand 55-meter brick temple dates to 5th–6th century CE Gupta era
Maurya and Gupta dynasties; inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2002
Shelters the sacred Bodhi Tree (Ficus religiosa) and the diamond throne (Vajrasana) marking the seat of Enlightenment

name: Nalanda Mahavihara Ruins
summary: Ancient international residential Buddhist university that flourished for 700 years.
points: Established in the 5th century CE under Gupta Emperor Kumaragupta I; supported by Emperor Harsha and Pala kings
Gupta and Pala dynasties; UNESCO World Heritage Site
Accommodated 10,000 students and 2,000 teachers from China, Korea, Japan, and Central Asia before sacking in 1193 CE
